verdicts.misleading_risk: One of the three quoted README statements is wrong. VLab4Mic's README on main (line 39) says 'macOS | .pkg (ARM64 or Intel) or .sh | Pick ARM64 for Apple silicon, Intel otherwise.' I found no 'M1 or newer; Intel Macs are not supported' text anywhere in the clones. Cited as written, the proposal would make the site say the authors do not support Intel for an app whose README says they do. The unsupported-Intel statements are verified only for GuessTheCondition (README:49) and Playground (README:32). The proposal's default text 'Supported systems: not stated by the authors' on every app page without the field would be noise on all six apps, and would read as a warning about an app that is fine. The jsonld operatingSystem 'Windows, macOS, Linux' stays true for a Mac-arm64-only app, so that point is cosmetic.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Real gap for two apps: GuessTheCondition and Playground pages show an Intel .pkg button, with the hint 'Intel, or M1 and later', while their READMEs say Intel Macs are unsupported. Drop the VLab4Mic claim. Do this in order. (1) Cheapest and most honest: those two apps stop building the Intel installer. The template workflow has a fixed matrix with a macos-intel entry (LabConstrictor/.github/workflows/release_constructor.yml:93). The site already shows only what the release contains, so nothing changes here. Make that opt-out a documented step in the template guide. (2) Only if the owners want authors to say it explicitly: add an optional manifest field `platforms` (enum windows-x86_64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64, linux-x86_64), small and author-controlled. When it is present, os_button and downloads_table skip unlisted assets and the macOS tile shows the author-stated line 'Intel Macs: not supported by this app's authors'. When it is absent, change nothing and print no new line. Do not add a 'not stated' line. Derive jsonld operatingSystem from the offered systems only if the field exists. Tests: field present, field absent, unsupported system with an asset in the release. The app manifests change in their own repos, not here.
verdicts.evidence: Built site shows Intel .pkg in the snapshot for all six apps (assets list macos x86_64 pkg primary for each). cards.py:107-117 downloads() builds tiles from assets. pages_apps.py:64-68 os_tile hint reads 'Intel, or M1 and later'. Schema properties list has no platforms field. GuessTheCondition/README.md:49 and LabConstrictor-Playground/README.md:32 state Intel unsupported on main. LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic main README:39 says 'ARM64 or Intel', which contradicts the gap. pages_apps.py:184-185 sets operatingSystem. I did not test whether the Intel installer runs.

verdicts.misleading_risk: The proposed sentence 'The installer was installed and the app opened' and the 'Install tested' rename describe a maintainer procedure that is not written down anywhere, so the site would be inventing a definition. The `by` login and the systems list are new claims nobody currently makes. 'Community listing' wording is safe, because it describes what the build checks, which is verifiable in catalogue.py and validate.py. Adding a schema object for a dormant tier (no registry file has verified_version) is overbuilding.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Fix the wording and placement now. Leave the tier schema alone until a maintainer actually verifies an app. (1) Write the definitions once, as a short 'How to read the labels' section in content/guides/using-apps.md. It says: Community means the automatic checks (public repository, valid manifest, installers from the app's own GitHub release); it is not a claim about scientific correctness, installer safety, or running on your system. Verified means a maintainer installed and ran that exact version. Whether 'ran' also covers opening the app is for the owners to confirm. LEGEND becomes one sentence plus a link, submit.md:48-49 links to the section instead of repeating it, and the header chip becomes a link to the section. (2) Rename the details row 'Status' to 'Listing' (it holds the tier, pages_apps.py:145) and use the 'does not say the results are correct' sentence in it. (3) Give the Community chip a visibly different style from the route chips Desktop and Colab. Update the DESIGN.md:49 colour rule in the same change. (4) Schema: make verified_on required together with verified_version (dependentRequired), and add an optional `verified_systems` list only when the first real verification is recorded, with the sentence 'Verified for 0.1.5 on macOS 14 (Apple Silicon), 9 October 2026'. (5) For a superseded verification show 'Last verified: 0.1.4, 1 September 2026 (not the current release)' instead of erasing it. Owners decide whether to rename the 'Verified' chip to 'Install tested'.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low if the label is derived from the plugin's status. The risk is conflating the plugin's maturity with the app's own tool: an app's `hosts` entry is the author's claim, the plugin status is the plugin's. Wording must say 'plugin' (for example 'napari plugin: experimental') so the site does not assert that this app's tools were tested in napari. 'Available' is a claim only when the plugin repo says so. The status vocabulary has four values (Experimental, Available, Install from GitHub, Deprecated), and each needs a defined string.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Build it, smaller. (1) Replace the hard-coded 'Soon in X' (cards.py:62-71) with text derived from the plugin's docs/labconstrictor-project.yaml status. data/hosts.yaml already names the plugin repo, and build/sources already holds the fetched project files. Map the four values to strings: 'napari plugin: experimental', 'napari plugin: available', 'napari plugin: install from GitHub', 'napari plugin: deprecated'. An unreadable or invalid status stops the build with an error naming the repo (AGENTS.md rule), no fallback to 'Soon'. (2) Card chips stay logo-only on small screens. Make the title and sr-only text carry the derived label, and add one visible word ('Experimental') only if the card width allows. I could not verify that on a rendered card. (3) Rename the filter and details row 'Works in' to 'Also in' with 'plugin' wording (pages_apps.py:27,147). (4) Fix the home line and the hero so they match: data/site.yaml:8 says 'Soon, apps can also work inside...' and pages_site.py:65 says 'Apps that declare tools also run inside...'. Use one sentence in both, for example 'Experimental plugins let apps that declare tools run in napari, Fiji and QuPath.' (5) Update DESIGN.md:45 and :49, and tests/test_site.py:213 and tests/test_design.py:61-62, in the same change. No new manifest field.
verdicts.evidence: cards.py:62-71 hard-codes 'Soon in'. data/site.yaml:8 reads 'Soon, apps can also work inside napari, Fiji and QuPath.' and pages_site.py:65 reads 'Apps that declare tools also run inside ...'. The built VLab4Mic page contains 'Soon in napari', 'Soon in Fiji', 'Two of its tools also run in Napari and Fiji.' and 'Works in'. The three plugin docs/labconstrictor-project.yaml files say status: Experimental. The napari user guide says 'Under heavy construction... untested' and 'Tested on Linux. Windows and macOS are untested.' The snapshot shows hosts napari/fiji on Guess the Condition and VLab4Mic, and napari/fiji/qupath on Playground.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Moderate. A status the author writes ('stable') is shown as an author claim, so the label must say 'stated by the authors', not appear as the site's judgement. Four values overlap: 'experimental' and 'in-development' are hard to tell apart, and 'discontinued' conflicts with the site's rule that an archived repository is silently unlisted (catalogue.py:26-27), so it would be rarely seen. Printing 'not stated' on all six pages is honest, but the gain is small until authors fill the field in. Renaming the chip 'Testing' to 'Not for analysis' is accurate to the section text, not invented.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Build a smaller version. (1) Optional manifest `status` with three values: stable, experimental, discontinued. Use the plugin vocabulary where it overlaps, so the site has one maturity word list. Show it in Details as 'Development status (stated by the authors)'. When it is absent, show 'Not stated' like License does. No chip for stable. Add a chip for experimental and discontinued. (2) Rename the grey 'Testing' chip to 'For testing', with title 'Checks or demonstrates LabConstrictor itself', and move one sentence of the section text next to the chip. (3) submit_app.py adds a warning (not an error) when status is missing, like the icon warning. Do not make it required: that would delist all six apps, so defer that to a later schema version. (4) Rename the 'Status' row to 'Listing' (shared with gap 2). Update DESIGN.md:49 (grey = Testing). Template guide and initialiser form changes are in other repos and are the owners' call. Drop 'in-development' and the ready-made sentences like 'Check results yourself', which are the site's opinion.

No status or maturity field; required is schema, name, summary, kind, distribution. Plugin schema has the status enum Experimental/Available/Install from GitHub/Deprecated. cards.py:74-76 testing_badge. pages_apps.py:145 'Status' holds the tier.
